profiles.meeting_scenario: Two ML research collaborators are holding a 10-turn brainstorming meeting to generate a workshop-paper idea inspired by the review on Evolved Plastic Artificial Neural Networks (EPANNs). The context is that their lab wants a compact but conceptually fresh project that can be prototyped in six weeks using existing infrastructure from prior meta-learning and open-ended evolution work. Their agenda is to identify one promising framing, sketch what kind of benchmark and training loop would demonstrate it, and decide what a minimal first prototype should look like. The expected outcome is informal convergence on a candidate direction they can pitch to the PI as a 'small but novel EPANN revival' project.

members.name: Dr. Maya Chen
members.expertise: neuroevolution, continual adaptation, biologically inspired learning systems
members.background: Maya runs a small academic lab focused on adaptive agents and previously published on differentiable plasticity and population-based training for embodied RL tasks.
members.private_state: She wants a workshop-paper concept that sounds genuinely new to reviewers without requiring a large engineering lift, and she is quietly trying to reuse the lab's existing maze-agent infrastructure rather than launch a new systems effort.
hidden_assumptions: A 'plastic network' in this project naturally means a standard forward network augmented with local lifetime weight updates, not architecture growth or developmental morphology changes.
If they say 'evolution' for a fast-turnaround paper, it is obvious they mean optimizing plasticity-rule parameters and initial conditions over a population of lightweight runs on existing RL tasks.
A result is 'adaptive' if an agent measurably improves within an episode or over a short sequence of related episodes without gradient updates at deployment time.
A 'minimal prototype' should stay inside the lab's current gridworld and memory task suite, because changing environments or simulators would dominate the timeline.

members.name: Leo Alvarez
members.expertise: meta-learning, foundation-model evaluation, evolutionary search over learning algorithms
members.background: Leo recently worked on in-context learning probes and is interested in using modern sequence models to revisit old adaptive-agent ideas in a way that feels relevant to current ML audiences.
members.private_state: He wants the brainstorm to produce a project that can bridge classic EPANN ideas with modern model-based or sequence-model narratives, ideally positioning his dissertation around 'evolved learning dynamics' rather than another small RL paper.
hidden_assumptions: A 'plastic network' in a modern EPANN revival can include fast stateful adaptation in activations, memory slots, or recurrent context, not only explicit synaptic weight changes.

When discussing 'evolution,' it is natural to include offline search over update programs, controller motifs, and prompt-like or sequence-level adaptation mechanisms, even if implemented in a transformer-style architecture.
Calling a system 'adaptive' implies showing transfer to held-out task families or shifts that were not structurally identical to the training distribution.

A 'minimal prototype' can still count as minimal if it uses an existing sequence-model codebase and a new synthetic task generator, because that is less conceptually constraining than reusing old gridworlds.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as a plastic network
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both say they want to test a 'plastic network' or 'plastic component.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means explicit synaptic plasticity: network weights or Hebbian-style traces that change during an agent's lifetime according to local update rules.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means any fast adaptive internal mechanism, including recurrent hidden-state updates, external memory writes, or sequence-conditioned behavior that effectively changes computation during deployment.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In EPANN discussions, 'plasticity' is often invoked at a high conceptual level, and both mechanisms plausibly fit the biological inspiration story, so the phrase feels aligned without forcing operational clarification.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to start with a 'minimal prototype' before scaling.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes minimal means reusing the lab's existing gridworld/continual-RL benchmark suite, code wrappers, and analysis scripts with only a small plasticity module added.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes minimal means the smallest conceptually clean demonstration, even if it requires spinning up a fresh synthetic task generator in a language-model or sequence-model codebase.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both hear 'minimal' as a sensible constraint on effort, but one is minimizing engineering change while the other is minimizing conceptual baggage; that distinction is rarely verbalized in early brainstorming.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They both want evidence that the system 'adapts online' or shows 'real adaptation.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 would count adaptation as rapid within-lifetime improvement on recurrent task structures in the same benchmark family, such as faster maze solving after early failures within an episode block.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 would count adaptation only if the learned dynamics help on genuinely held-out task families or distribution shifts, not merely repeated structures from the same generator.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are invoking a high-status research goal with the same phrase, and in brainstorming it sounds premature to pin down exact evaluation boundaries, so the different standards stay latent.

misalignment_points.topic: What kind of evolution they are reusing
misalignment_points.surface_form: They refer to 'the old evolution loop' or 'our population setup' as something they can leverage.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the lab's existing neuroevolution pipeline for PPO-initialized maze agents with population-level search over plasticity coefficients.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of a separate offline evolutionary-search framework he used last year to mutate compact update programs over sequence models on synthetic algorithmic tasks.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both have previously discussed 'evolutionary search' in shared lab spaces, and each assumes the other is invoking the most relevant prior system; the reference feels specific enough to avoid suspicion but is actually ambiguous.

Ideally this is a workshop paper built on the maze and memory benchmarks we already have, with a small add-on for lifetime plasticity and no major systems rebuild. If Leo has a framing that sounds current, great, but I want the minimal prototype to stay inside our existing suite.

The modern hook is that evolution discovers the adaptation strategy itself.
